input.question: In medical terms, what is a triage?
input.ground_truth: In it's simplest form, it's prioritizing. You sort patients - meaning you triage them- based on severity so that you can determine the priority of care. That means you've got women with splinters on one end of the triage spectrum, and a 70 year old man with coronary failure on the other.

Okay! Imagine you and your friends are all hurt a little bit after playing outside. Some of you have really big hurts, like a scraped knee, and some have just a tiny boo-boo.

A **triage** is when a grown-up (like a nurse or doctor) looks at everyone and decides who needs help the most right away. They help the people who are the most hurt first, so they don't get worse. Then they help the others after that.

So, **triage** is a way to decide who needs help the fastest when lots of people are hurt or sick.
